claims.statement: Learners use a causal window split: the default learn window is 2026-04-14 → 2026-08-15 (end day padded to 23:59:59) for both learners, and replay windows (defaults 08-16 → 09-18 for W1 replay, 08-16 → 09-19 for W2) are strictly later; no learner learns from, or a replay gate evaluates, events outside its own window (因果切分：回放只用后续窗口).

The learning population is self-contained complete journeys: a car contributes only if both its first entry event (01IS205/1L360RB/01IS045) and first exit event (K3IS140/1J440RB/K2IS075/K1IS135) fall inside the window (exit_t > entry_t); in-progress cars truncated by the window boundary are excluded from the sample.

sqlbase.ev_base_sql is the single shared extraction caliber for both learners and all replays (DRY): one execute of a multi-statement SQL that builds three session TEMP tables (tmp_w4_p = one scan of product cars BODY_ID LIKE '78202%%' in window with bits 137/139 extracted; tmp_loop_bounds = dual-loop boundaries; tmp_ev_base = purified event base); TEMP tables are session-scoped, so all learning queries must run on the same connection that built them.

tmp_ev_base purifies the flag into {'0','1','2'}: events inside the pure rework window [t_rw_start, t_rw_end] become '1' (priority), inside the pure blacktop window [t_bt_start, t_bt_end] become '2' (t_bt_start requires 137=1 AND 139=2 at/after first oven-out of 16IS305/17IS305/18IS345), everything else '0'; loop ends are the first pass of the gateway group 25IS010/25IS110/25IS210 after tagging (NULL = no gateway); last_loop_t keeps the byte-identical max(t) FILTER (flag IN ('1','2')) OVER (PARTITION BY body) expression so clean-suffix exclusion semantics of W1/W2 consumers are unchanged.

The W1 learner implements the five-step pipeline 过滤 → 分段 → 清洗 → 聚合 → 自校准 as SQL over the ev_base foundation: main() executes DDL → ev_base build → platform-prefix discovery → four distribution INSERTs → dim_loop_duration → meta → sanity checks S1–S6 → sanity report → exit 0 if all pass else 1.

Every W1 distribution table carries three tiers of rows (model body_type, platform prefix LEFT(bt,2), 'ALL') and the prefix list is discovered at runtime, never hardcoded: distinct LEFT(bt,2) with at least 30 distinct vehicles in the learn window (SQL_PLATFORM_PREFIXES); prefix_in_list rejects tokens not matching ^[A-Z0-9]{2}$ (injection guard) and an empty list degrades to model + ALL rows only.

dim_station_takt cleaning is a per-bucket IQR rule (keep dur <= q3 + 3×(q3−q1)) computed independently per tier (model/prefix/ALL each with its own fences); night-stop (夜停) cross-window gaps have no explicit time-band removal and are absorbed by the in-bucket outlier exclusion; the overall exclusion rate is recorded in meta as takt_iqr_excl_rate.

dim_remaining_time aggregates the clean-suffix population (flag='0', t < exit_t, last_loop_t IS NULL OR t > last_loop_t) and dim_loop_remaining the loop population (flag IN ('1','2'), t < exit_t); both emit P50 (percentile_cont 0.5), mean, P90 (percentile_cont 0.9) and n per (tier, station) key with n always the last column.

dim_future_flag p1/p2 are the shares of clean-suffix events (flag='0', t < exit_t) for which the body's first flag=1 / first flag=2 time lies strictly after the event; the join to per-body first-flag times is materialized once in the j CTE because per-branch joins made the planner choose a Nested Loop (outer ff × materialized tmp_ev_base, ~3.68M rows re-scanned, >600 s timeout), while the single-join form took ~6 s via hash join (W4.2b 实测坑, 2026-10-05).

dim_loop_duration follows the W4.2a contract: per-vehicle L is the pure window duration from tmp_loop_bounds (rw: t_rw_end − t_rw_start; bt: t_bt_end − t_bt_start), a NULL end falling back to the car's exit_t (JOINed from tmp_ev_base because the bounds table has no exit column); rows are a 4-tuple (l = P50 compatibility name, l_mean, l_p90, n) so consumers reading row[0]/row[-1] are unchanged, and the legacy max(t) − min(t) suffix method was removed.

W1 exits 0 only if all sanity gates S1–S6 pass (else 1) and always writes output/w1_learn_sanity_<YYYYMMDD>.md first: S1 entry-station P50 8–30 h + rem ≤ journey P50 + deviation ≤ max(10%, 1.5× W1 closeout baseline) with 01IS045 report-only; S2a first flag=1 in the rework cluster ≥ 80%; S2b blacktop anchor placement rate ≥ 90% on the 10-station whitelist; S2c p1 profile (n ≥ 1000 stations) max ≥ 0.03 and min ≤ 0.01; S3 loop_duration ALL-row n flag1 ≥ 8500 / flag2 ≥ 4000; S4 loop-event counts measured on tmp_ev_base flag1 ≥ 180,000 / flag2 ≥ 80,000; S5 takt IQR exclusion ≤ 0.30; S6 clean-suffix rate ≥ 0.80 under purified semantics.

S2b was replaced (not recalibrated) at W4.2d: under purification the old rule (first flag=2 concentrated in BLACKTOP_CLUSTER ('14IS260','24IS185') ≥ 60%) must fail because the 14IS260 false blacktop is purified to '0'; the new S2b is the t_bt_start anchor placement rate ≥ 90% on a 10-station whitelist (post-oven report-entry cluster + polishing line, identical to the online BLACKTOP_ONLINE_WHITELIST), with no code residue of the old rule.

S3/S4 thresholds were recalibrated at W4.2d for the post-purification sample drop (transition baseline = new measured × 92% margin): S3 flag1 ≥ 8,500 ∧ flag2 ≥ 4,000 (measured 9,351 / 4,356 cars), S4 flag1 ≥ 180,000 ∧ flag2 ≥ 80,000 (measured 192,197 / 86,210 events); the old thresholds (S3 9000/7000, S4 250,000/100,000, calibrated on the legacy suffix method) were removed; S4's metric is measured directly from tmp_ev_base because SUM(n) over three-tier table rows double-counts (~2×); S5 is unchanged (population unchanged) and S6 keeps 0.80 with updated semantics.

W1 S1 was calibrated at W4.2e against the W1 closeout baseline (in-code citation of output/w1-验证摘要.md L38): 01IS045 became report-only (small-sample substitute entry station that had FAILed since the W1 closeout) and the consistency band became max(10%, 1.5× closeout measured deviation) (01IS205 11.6% / 1L360RB 30.9%) because the clean-suffix population is structurally lower than the full journey population, making the original 10% threshold unreachable by design; the rem ≤ journey direction check is retained.

The W2-S2 threshold was lowered from n ≥ 1000 to n ≥ 300 at the W2 closeout (2026-09-21): the 8-week rolling window measured n = 343–810 for the 15IS065 decision cluster, so the old 1000 was a spec residue mismatched with the window scale; after the fix W2-S1–S4 all PASS and the learner exits 0.

The W2 learner writes only the six dss.v2_* tables plus the two W4 net-delay tables; the six W1 dss.dim_* tables (including meta) are read-only inputs (regression guardrail), and W1 must be re-learned first with the same learn window because dim_expected_delay reads the same-source baseline (p50) from dss.dim_remaining_time.

W2 main() order: DDL → full-window ev_base → v2_future_flag/v2_line_prob (week 'ALL') → v2_cohort_remaining → dim_expected_delay → dim_expected_delay_shift (both must run after the full-window ev_base and before the week loop, which rebuilds tmp_ev_base) → per-replay-week loop (ev_base rebuilt on the rolling window, then weekly p and line probability) → build_quality (Python side) → meta → W2-S1–S5 gates (exit 0 only if all pass) + report.

Weekly p (v2_future_flag) is learned on the ⑥a purified pre-loop population — flag=0, t < exit_t, and before the body's first flag=1 and first flag=2 — excluding loop-then-back-to-mainline cars and inter-loop events, so p = P(future loop entry | currently pre-loop); each replay-week row is learned on a rolling 8-week window strictly preceding that week (shifts.week_learning_range = [Monday − 8 weeks, Monday − 1 day], no future leak), plus full-window week='ALL' rows.

v2_cohort_remaining covers the 08IS/09IS parallel-line split: shared stations (not 08IS/09IS-prefixed) × the line a car later took, restricted to single-line cars (c08 XOR c09, cohort '08'/'09'); the cohort must be computed on tmp_ev_base, not the raw stream, because post-exit record stations 09IS360/09IS350 would pollute LIKE '09IS%%'; v2_line_prob gives per-model weekly + ALL w08 (08IS share) as the cohort fallback-chain endpoint.

Station quality marks and the compensation exemption set are derived Python-side: v2_station_quality marks model×station cells (2-char prefix rows excluded from marking) as low_n (model row n < 30), mixed (p1 ≥ 0.5), both, or ok, with p1 from v2_future_flag week='ALL' (missing model row falls back to the station ALL row); v2_comp_excl is exactly the 'both' cells (⑥b: mixed low-n stations exempt from compensation); cells with no model row are left unmarked, defaulting to 'ok' in the engine.

dim_expected_delay (W4.2c, doc10 §2) is computed on the ⑥a pre-loop population (same population and window as v2_future_flag week='ALL'; the clean-suffix population is structurally disjoint from fut=1 and must not be used): fut=1 = the body's first flag=1 lies after the event; base = COALESCE of model→prefix→ALL p50 from W1 dim_remaining_time with n ≥ 30 gates on all three LEFT JOINs; delay_mean_s = max(0, P(fut)×mean(rem−base | fut=1) + (mean(rem_clean) − p50(rem_clean))) and delay_p50_s = max(0, P(fut)×p50(rem−base | fut=1)) with outer truncation only and the correction term entering only the mean column; a row is written only if both sample_n (fut=1) and sample_n_clean (fut=0) are ≥ 30 (dual population dual gate), else the engine degrades model→prefix→ALL→0; the prefix tier uses all LEFT(bt,2) prefixes without the platform whitelist.

dim_expected_delay_shift (W4.4h) applies the same discipline with an added shift dimension: sample attribution is the entry-event shift (entry minutes-of-day in [285, 989] i.e. 04:45–16:30 → 'DAY', else 'MID' covering [16:30, 04:45) with the low-activity tail gap folded into MID — the same attribution windows as spike_w2/shifts.py); P(fut) reuses the non-shift-conditioned v2_future_flag; the table is optional — absent rows make the engine resolver fall back to the shared row, and it is consumed only when DSS_SHIFT_TIER_DELAY=1.

coverage_gaps(p1_cells, delay_rows, p1_threshold=0.10) is the pure coverage-gap monitor: a (model, station) cell with p1 ≥ 0.10 where none of the model / prefix / ALL tiers has a delay row is a gap (engine falls back to 0 = pure under-estimation risk, which doc10 §2.3 requires monitoring); results are sorted by p1 descending and the learner report lists the top-30 gaps.

Learner DDL is DROP TABLE IF EXISTS + CREATE TABLE per table: each run is a full rebuild of the tables owned by that learner, executed inside the dss-only write boundary (ods/dim/fct/mart/meta layers are strictly read-only; the dss schema may be dropped and recreated).

DB-connected learner scripts are launched as conda run --no-capture-output -n paint-dss python <script> (Windows discipline): directly invoking the env interpreter crashed at psycopg2.connect with an access violation (exit -1073741819 = 0xC0000005, non-deterministic, DLL/PATH dependent), so that older guidance is void; python -c under conda run is single-line only (multi-line code goes in a script file); the M5 production sequence runs 01_learn_takt.py then 01_learn_v2.py back-to-back to rebuild the 14 learning tables.

Exit-code convention: learners exit 1 when any sanity gate fails (exit 0 = all gates PASS; the sanity report is written in both cases), while exit 2 is the reporting convention reserved for replay gate scripts (02_*, exit 0 过 / exit 2 未过); the 'ERROR conda.cli... failed' line conda run prints on a non-zero exit is that reporting artifact, not a crash — judge by the produced artifact.

Both learners connect through spike_w1/common.py::connect(): psycopg2 with autocommit=True and session SET TIME ZONE 'Asia/Shanghai' (factory time = UTC+8, mandatory), with the DSN resolved fresh at each call so DSS_DB_HOST/PORT/NAME/USER/PASSWORD env overrides take effect at runtime (defaults: dev DB 127.0.0.1/root/root, .env loaded via python-dotenv); the W2 module reuses this W1 connection helper.

tests/test_w4_learn_takt.py and tests/test_w4_learn_v2.py are pure no-DB contract tests (real-DB re-learning verification is the separate W4.2e step): they load the learner modules via importlib.import_module('spike_w1.01_learn_takt') / importlib.import_module('spike_w2.01_learn_v2') and pin DDL shapes, SQL text contracts (loop-bounds L semantics, per-tier IQR fences, single-join future-flag, three-tier prefix patterns, net-delay formula/dual-gate/truncation counts), sanity source contracts (S2b replacement, S3/S4 recalibration, S1/S6 semantics), the w4_meta_rows pure function, the coverage_gaps pure function, and the ordering that SQL_EXPECTED_DELAY executes after the full-window ev_base and before the week loop.
